newsitem.title: USA: N.J. candidate urges higher cigarette tax -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. candidate urges higher cigarette tax -- paper.

text.p: A candidate hoping to unseat New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman proposed increasing the state's cigarette tax to pay for pre-school classes and other services in urban schools, the Bergen Record reported Tuesday.
Democratic candidate Michael Murphy called for the tax increase to reverse what he called a decline in state support for education under the current Republican administration.
Murphy said a 25-cent increase in the tobacco tax could generate $150 million a year for schools.
A similar plan proposed by a Republican lawmaker last year failed when Whitman declined to endorse it.
Whitman herself last year proposed using higher cigarette taxes to pay for uninsured workers' health coverage, but that idea also failed when the legislature balked.
